# 2 Kings Chapter 1 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 222r–222v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2KI_001_page_001.jpg, 2KI_001_page_002.jpg

---

**1:1** And-rebelled Moav against-Yisra'el after the-death of-Achav.

**1:2** And-fell Achazyahu through the-lattice [ha-sevakhah] in-his-upper-room that [was] in-Shomron, and-was-sick. And-sent messengers and-said to-them: Go, inquire of-Ba'al-Zevuv, god of-Eqron, whether I-shall-recover from-this sickness.

**1:3** And-[the]-angel of-YHWH spoke to-Eliyahu the-Tishbite: Arise, go-up to-meet the-messengers of-[the]-king of-Shomron, and-speak to-them: Is-it because-there-is-no [ha-mi-beli] God in-Yisra'el [that] you-are-going to-inquire of-Ba'al-Zevuv, god of-Eqron?

**1:4** And-therefore, thus says YHWH: The-bed upon which you-have-gone-up, you-shall-not come-down from-it, for you-shall-surely-die [mot tamut]. And-went Eliyahu.

**1:5** And-returned the-messengers to-him, and-he-said to-them: Why [is] this [that] you-have-returned?

**1:6** And-they-said to-him: A-man came-up to-meet-us and-said to-us: Go, return to the-king who sent you, and-speak to-him: Thus says YHWH: Is-it because-there-is-no God in-Yisra'el [that] you-are-sending to-inquire of-Ba'al-Zevuv, god of-Eqron? Therefore, the-bed upon which you-have-gone-up, you-shall-not come-down from-it, for you-shall-surely-die.

**1:7** And-he-spoke to-them: What [was] the-manner [mishpat] of-the-man who came-up to-meet you and-spoke to-you these words?

**1:8** And-they-said to-him: A-man, a-possessor of-hair [ba'al se'ar], and-a-belt of-leather [ezor or] girded on-his-loins. And-he-said: He [is] Eliyahu the-Tishbite.

**1:9** And-he-sent to-him a-captain of-fifty [sar chamishim] and-his-fifty. And-he-went-up to-him, and-behold, he [was] sitting upon the-top of-the-mountain. And-he-spoke to-him: Man of-God [ish ha-elohim], the-king has-spoken — come-down!

**1:10** And-answered Eliyahu and-spoke to the-captain of-the-fifty: And-if I [am] a-man of-God, let-fire come-down from the-heavens and-consume you and-your-fifty. And-came-down fire from the-heavens and-consumed him and-his-fifty.

**1:11** And-he-returned and-sent to-him another captain of-fifty and-his-fifty. And-he-answered and-spoke to-him: Man of-God, thus says the-king — come-down quickly [meherah]!

**1:12** And-answered Eliyahu and-spoke to-them: If I [am] a-man of-God, let-fire come-down from the-heavens and-consume you and-your-fifty. And-came-down fire of-God from the-heavens and-consumed him and-his-fifty.

**1:13** And-he-returned and-sent a-captain of-a-third fifty and-his-fifty. And-went-up and-came the-captain of-the-third fifty and-knelt upon his-knees before Eliyahu, and-pleaded [vayitchannen] to-him, and-spoke to-him: Man of-God, let-be-precious please [tiqar na] my-life [nafshi] and-the-life of-your-servants, these fifty, in-your-eyes.

**1:14** Behold, fire came-down from the-heavens and-consumed the-two former captains of-fifties and-their-fifties; and-now, let-my-life be-precious in-your-eyes.

**1:15** And-spoke the-angel of-YHWH to-Eliyahu: Go-down with-him; do-not be-afraid of-him [al tira mipanav]. And-he-arose and-went-down with-him to the-king.

**1:16** And-he-spoke to-him: Thus says YHWH: Because you-sent messengers to-inquire of-Ba'al-Zevuv, god of-Eqron — is-it because-there-is-no God in-Yisra'el to-inquire of-his-word? — therefore the-bed upon which you-have-gone-up, you-shall-not come-down from-it, for you-shall-surely-die.

**1:17** And-he-died according-to-the-word of-YHWH that Eliyahu had-spoken. And-Yehoram reigned in-his-place, in-the-second year of-Yehoram son of-Yehoshafat, king of-Yehudah, because he-had no son.

**1:18** And-the-rest of-the-deeds of-Achazyahu that he-did, are-they not written in the-book of-the-chronicles [divrey ha-yamim] of-the-kings of-Yisra'el?

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.2 — Ba'al-Zevuv:** Literally "Lord of the Flies" — the Ekronite deity. This may be a deliberate Hebrew distortion of the original name Ba'al-Zebul ("Lord Prince" or "Lord of the Exalted Dwelling"). The theological question — "Is there no God in Israel?" — is the refrain of the chapter (vv.3, 6, 16).

**v.8 — ba'al se'ar:** Literally "a possessor of hair" — describing Elijah as a hairy man, or possibly referring to a garment of hair (a prophet's mantle). The leather belt (*ezor or*) becomes iconic prophetic garb.

**v.10 — fire from the heavens:** The verbal echo of 1 Kings 18:38 (Carmel) is unmistakable. The same God who answered by fire on Carmel answers by fire on the mountain.

**v.13 — vayitchannen:** The hitpael of *chanan* — an intensified plea for grace. The third captain does what the first two refused to do: he acknowledges that this is genuinely a "man of God," not a subject to be commanded.

**v.17 — Yehoram:** A synchronism problem: two Jehorams reign simultaneously — one in Israel, one in Judah. The text handles this matter-of-factly.

*— EMET*
